oil.when: 2027, using the steering-wheel buttons and the Vehicle Maintenance menu
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have actually been changed.
With the vehicle on, use the steering-wheel buttons to open the main menu in the instrument cluster display.
Select Vehicle Maintenance, then select Oil Life.
Press and hold OK until the display confirms the reset.

oil.when: 2021, using the steering-wheel arrow and OK buttons
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the ignition on and open the main menu in the instrument cluster with the steering-wheel arrow buttons.
Scroll to Settings, then to Vehicle, and find the oil life item.
Press and hold OK while the cluster shows Hold OK to Reset.
Let go when it shows Reset Successful and oil life reads 100%. If it shows Not Reset or Reset Cancelled, go through the steps again.

oil.when: 2000 with the message center and OIL CHANGE RESET control
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the ignition on.
Press and hold the OIL CHANGE RESET control for about five seconds. The message center counts down while you hold it.
Let go when the message center shows OIL LIFE RESET TO 100% (or the starting percentage you set earlier).
Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker.
Drive above 20 mph for at least two minutes. The light should go out by itself.
If the tires are set correctly, the spare is not in use, and the light stays on, have the system checked.
tpms.note: If the light flashes for about a minute at start-up and then stays on, the system has a fault that adding air will not fix. The manual also calls for a system reset after every tire rotation; ask the tire shop or dealer to do it. After using the tire sealant kit, a dealer must replace that wheel's sensor and valve stem.

tpms.when: 2021: light clears after a short drive; after every tire rotation, retrain the sensors with the hazard-flasher method
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker.
If you only added air, drive above 20 mph for at least two minutes. The light should go out by itself.
After a tire rotation, drive above 20 mph for at least two minutes, then park safely where you can reach every tire with an air hose.
Turn the ignition off, then back on without starting the engine.
Within 10 seconds, turn the hazard flashers on and off three times. The horn sounds once, the tire pressure light flashes and a message appears.
Start at the left front tire: take off the valve cap and let air out slowly until the horn sounds once.
Repeat on the right front, then the right rear, then the left rear. Training is done after the horn sounds for the left rear.
Turn the ignition off. If you hear two short horn beeps at any point, the reset failed; start again.
Set all four tires back to the door-sticker pressure.
tpms.note: If the light flashes for about a minute at start-up and then stays on, the system has a fault that adding air or this reset will not clear. If the horn never sounds at the start after a second try, see a dealer.

notes: Explorer uses a calculated oil life reminder, so it will not clear itself after an oil change. The menu path changed between the 2021 and 2027 manuals.
